styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Museums, the Tower, Westminster and the West End stage.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Markets, pubs and a world of restaurants.

styles.label: Family
styles.blurb: Free museums, parks and the South Bank.

stays.why: Walk to theatres, Oxford Street and most central sights. Busy and noisy at night; book early.
Next to the Natural History and Science Museums and Hyde Park. Quiet streets, good for families.
Riverside walks, the Eye and the Tower within reach. Good Tube links from Waterloo and London Bridge.
The British Museum, the British Library and fast trains from King's Cross and St Pancras.

food: Try a proper Sunday roast in a pub, and fish and chips from a chippy. Expect roughly £12–20 a main.
Markets are the best value: Borough Market for snacks, Brick Lane for curry, Camden for street food.
Book popular restaurants ahead, especially for dinner Thursday to Saturday.
Lunch is often cheaper than dinner at the same place; many pubs do good-value set lunches.
Tap water is safe and free to ask for. A pint of beer is roughly £5–7 in central pubs.
more_time: Greenwich: take the Thames Clippers boat for the Cutty Sark, the market and the park.
Swap a museum day for a half-day trip to Hampton Court Palace or Kew Gardens by train.
Camden and Regent's Canal: walk the towpath from Camden Lock to Little Venice.

recommend.why: Three nights covers the big sights, a museum or two and a West End show without rushing.

month_notes: Jan: cold, highs near 8°C and about 12 rain days. Pack a warm coat.
Feb: still cold, highs near 9°C. Short days but quieter sights.
Mar: warming to about 11°C, but the wettest month with around 13 rain days.
Apr: mild at about 14°C. Good walking weather; showers possible.
May: pleasant highs near 17°C. A great month for parks and the river.
Jun: warm at about 21°C with long evenings. Busy season starts.
Jul: the warmest month, highs near 23°C. Book hotels and shows early.
Aug: warm at about 22°C. School holidays make sights crowded.
Sep: still mild near 20°C with fewer crowds. A strong month to visit.
Oct: cooling to about 16°C. Bring layers and a rain jacket.
Nov: chilly at about 11°C with around 12 rain days. Dark by late afternoon.
Dec: cold at about 9°C. Festive lights, short days, book ahead.

climate_guide.summary: Temperate and changeable: mild summers, cool winters, and rain in every month. Rarely extreme.

items.title: Rain all year
items.text: About 10–13 rain days every month. Showers are often short; carry a small umbrella or jacket.

items.title: Best time: May to September
items.text: Highs of 17–23°C and long daylight. July is warmest; September is mild with fewer crowds.

items.title: Winter is cool, not freezing
items.text: January and February highs near 8–9°C and lows near 2–3°C. A warm coat and layers are enough.

items.title: March is the wettest
items.text: Around 13 rain days. Plan indoor backups like museums and galleries.

items.title: Summer days are long
items.text: June to August gives the most daylight for parks, walks and the river. Evenings stay light.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers, a waterproof jacket and comfortable shoes for walking. Add sunglasses and a hat for summer.

transit.best: Contactless card on the Tube and buses; walk the centre.

modes.text: The Underground, Elizabeth line and Overground take contactless cards and Oyster. Fares are capped per day.
A flat £1.75 per bus, and a second bus within an hour is free (Hopper fare). Good for sightseeing above ground.
Black cabs are metered and can be hailed. Uber, Bolt and FREENOW are widely used.
Driving in the centre means the Congestion Charge and ULEZ fees. Visitors rarely need a car.
Central London is very walkable; many sights are 15–30 minutes apart on foot.
Thames Clippers river boats link Westminster, the South Bank, the Tower and Greenwich.
